content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to use an output from [product_name] for dimming LED strips through PWM? The module has transistor outputs and an SSR. What is the maximum switching speed for the transistor output?
Hello, according to the manual, the switching frequency of transistor outputs depends solely on the cycle time.

The cycle time is at least 1 second in total. The on/off duration can be split into 1000 steps. The combined on and off periods must be at least 1 second. This seems unsuitable for smooth operation with LED lamps.
Hi, refer to the [product_name] manual and technical specifications. The maximum switching frequency listed is around 10 Hz. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are investigating whether the transistor outputs of [product_name] modules support PWM dimming for LED strips. They wish to know about switching speed limitations. Feedback indicates that the shortest achievable cycle is 1 second, which allows segmenting for PWM purposes, but results in a low frequency that is not ideal for smooth LED dimming. Technical documentation suggests a maximum switching frequency of 10 Hz, which may lead to unsatisfactory results for this application.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to achieve smooth dimming of LED strips using PWM on [product_name] outputs, hoping for a sufficiently high switching speed.
